SHERPA TENSING'S TENSE GUIDE

SIMPLE: the whole event. CONTINUOUS, BE + -ING: in progress. PERFECT, HAVE + PAST PARTICIPLE: looking back from a point in time. In every question, read the time word first — "yesterday", "since seven", "by midnight".
Go to reception
ACT I · 19:40 · RECEPTION
Something outside the routine

Alice is teaching you the evening routine. Mrs Hudson checks the guest book. Holmes and Watson, who run the village investigation office, are here for dinner, not work. “The owner rings the desk every evening,” Alice says. “But look at his light. Someone is calling from his office right now.”
You answer. A voice whispers, “Don’t let them sell the hotel.” Then the line dies.
Describe the routine, then the action happening now: “The owner ___ every evening. Someone ___ from his office right now.”
Both forms are past. The sentence is about a routine and about this moment, so it needs present forms.
HAS CALLED is a result and CALLED is a finished past event. Neither says "every evening" or "right now".
This swaps the meanings. A routine takes the simple form, THE OWNER + CALLS; an action in progress takes the continuous.
"Every evening" is a routine: THE OWNER + CALLS. "Right now" is an action in progress: SOMEONE + IS CALLING.
ACT I · 19:50 · THE KEY DESK
A key without a room

Count Blocula, the hotel’s owner, arrives in an ivory dinner jacket. He gives you a brass key marked 309. “Keep this safe until I return.” Rabbit, the fast-moving bellhop, insists there are only two guest floors. Mouse, the smallest porter, nods. Security chief Lestrade checks the printed plan. No room 309.
“I saw that key yesterday,” Lestrade says. “But this is the first time the Count has given it to anyone.”
One event has a finished time; the other matters now: “Lestrade ___ the key yesterday. The Count ___ it to us, so we have it now.”
HAD SEEN needs an earlier past point, and HAS BEEN GIVING is an ongoing activity, not one handover.
One sighting is SAW, not WAS SEEING. GIVES is a routine, not one new handover.
"Yesterday" is a finished time, so SAW, not HAS SEEN. GAVE loses the link to now: we have the key.
"Yesterday" is a finished time: LESTRADE + SAW. A recent action with a result now: THE COUNT + HAS JUST GIVEN.
ACT I · 20:05 · THE FAREWELL BALLROOM
Eleven seconds of darkness

Zombiella reaches the last note of her song. Tito is at the piano. Blane, the night porter, carries a tray of glasses. Andreas, the hotel’s buyer, watches the owner instead of the stage. The lights go out. A tray crashes. Eleven seconds later, light returns.
Blocula’s chair is empty. An ivory envelope lies on the floor. Inside it you find a note: “At midnight, tell them what this building is really worth.”
Set the background, then name the interruption: “Zombiella ___ when the lights suddenly ___ out.”
The song was in progress: ZOMBIELLA + WAS SINGING. The blackout interrupted it: THE LIGHTS + WENT out.
HAD SUNG means the song was already over, but she was still singing. HAVE GONE links to now.
SANG makes the whole song one event, and WERE GOING makes the sudden blackout a long background action.
HAS SUNG and GO are present forms. The story is at 20:05, in the past.
ACT I · 20:12 · BEHIND THE STAGE
The first impossible alibi

Andreas says he left the ballroom at 20:10, after the blackout, and went directly to the terrace. He claims he has never used the service lift. Zombiella shows you a photo Rabbit took at 20:03. Andreas’s chair is empty. His coat is already gone. Tito remembers opening the service door for him before the lights failed.
“A confident voice is not a clock,” Holmes says. “Put the events in order.”
The photo is at 20:03; the blackout is at 20:05: “Andreas ___ the ballroom before the lights ___ out.”
WAS LEAVING puts him in the middle of leaving, and HAVE GONE links to now, not to 20:05.
HAS LEFT looks from now. Here we look back from 20:05, a finished past point.
The earlier event: ANDREAS + HAD ALREADY LEFT. The later event: THE LIGHTS + WENT out. His 20:10 story is false.
LEAVES is a present routine. We are putting two finished past events in order.
NOTEBOOK · THE 20:03 PHOTOGRAPH. Andreas had already left before the 20:05 blackout. His claimed 20:10 departure is false.
ACT I · 20:20 · SERVICE LIFT WORKSHOP
The man inside the lift

You find Zombito waist-deep in an open control cabinet. Jax holds a lamp. The Creature, the hotel’s enormous maintenance assistant, is supporting the lift door with one hand. Zombito looks alarming and sounds exhausted. “I started at seven. I’m still fixing this thing. I’ve replaced three fuses, but the door sensor keeps failing.”
There is a second fault: someone has removed a page from the lift’s paper log.
Focus first on ongoing effort, then completed results: “Zombito ___ since seven. He ___ three fuses so far.”
WORKED makes the work finished, and WAS REPLACING does not count three finished fuses.
HAS WORKED is possible, but HAS BEEN REPLACING is activity, not three finished results.
"Since seven" and still working: ZOMBITO + HAS BEEN WORKING. Three finished results: HE + HAS REPLACED.
IS WORKING cannot take "since seven", and REPLACED loses the link to now in "so far".
ACT I · 20:30 · THE COPPER KITCHEN
The kitchen knows everyone

Chef Mrs Hudson has sent Rafa, Silver and Jack to feed the frightened guests. Kit is checking meal deliveries. Henry Clerval, the hotel doctor’s assistant, makes tea for anyone who looks ready to faint. “I’ve known Andreas for ten years,” Hudson says. “He smiles like a man selling you your own shoes.”

Kit has counted every dinner tray. One extra meal went to the old east annex. Nobody has booked a room there. The Queen, the retired chairwoman, has sent her untouched pudding back. The Time Warden wants the staff to finish on schedule. Mrs Hudson ignores them both.
Choose a lasting state and an ongoing activity: “Hudson ___ Andreas for ten years. Kit ___ the deliveries all evening and is still checking.”
"Know" is a state, so the simple form: HUDSON + HAS KNOWN. Activity up to now: KIT + HAS BEEN CHECKING.
KNEW and HAD CHECKED move both facts into the past, but she still knows him and Kit is still checking.
"Know" is a state verb, so not HAS BEEN KNOWING. CHECKED says the checking is finished.
"Know" is a state verb, so not IS KNOWING. CHECKS is a routine, not tonight's activity.
ACT I · 20:40 · THE SECURITY CORRIDOR
The recording that arrived late

Lestrade’s camera uploads clips slowly in the storm. At 20:18, a recording finally arrived. It shows Blocula walking into the service lift at 20:04, carrying a folder. Blane insists he saw Andreas enter the same lift at 20:02. The camera confirms it. Andreas was already inside when the Count arrived.
Watson notices something else: the Count is smiling. He expected a meeting, not a kidnapping.
Report the order from a later past viewpoint: “By the time the Count ___ at 20:04, Andreas ___ the lift at 20:02.”
The later point: THE COUNT + ARRIVED. The earlier event: ANDREAS + HAD ENTERED.
ENTERS is present. We are telling the whole sequence in the past.
Both events have finished clock times, 20:02 and 20:04, so not HAS + past participle.
This puts HAD on the later event. The earlier one, the entry at 20:02, takes HAD ENTERED.
ACT I · 20:50 · THE WORKSHOP BENCH
A page in the rubbish

Victor Frankenstein, the hotel doctor, arrives with retired engineer Professor Waldman. Neither likes the smell of hot wires. The Creature finds the missing log page under a bin. The lift travelled to “E-309” at 20:06. The passenger doors opened, then someone locked the annex door from outside.
Zombito explains his own movements: he started repairing the panel at 19:00 and was still working there when the alarm rang at 20:05. Jax and the Creature were with him.
Look back from the alarm, then describe what was in progress: “Zombito ___ for over an hour when the alarm rang. At that moment, he ___ the panel.”
REPAIRED does not measure "for over an hour", and HAS CHECKED links to now, not to the alarm.
Activity up to a past event: ZOMBITO + HAD BEEN REPAIRING. In progress at that moment: HE + WAS CHECKING.
These forms look from now. Our point of view is the alarm at 20:05, in the past.
HAD CHECKED says the checking was already finished, but he was still doing it.
NOTEBOOK · THE TORN LIFT LOG. The lift reached E-309 at 20:06. Zombito was repairing the panel with two witnesses when the alarm rang.
ACT I · 21:00 · THE STAFF STAIR
Which witness gets your trust?

Zombiella says Andreas paid her to keep singing until 20:15, even if the lights failed. She thought it was a strange joke. Alice admits she copied an old annex key for him yesterday because he claimed the Count had asked for it. Both are frightened of losing their jobs. Both could help you.
You can ask Zombiella to search for the payment receipt, or ask Alice to trace the copied key. Your partner will bring a different piece of supporting evidence later.
Contrast a finished mistake with a problem that remains: “Alice ___ the key yesterday. Since then, she ___ unable to stop worrying.”
COPIES is a habit, and IS cannot carry "since then".
WAS COPYING is not one finished event, and HAD BEEN stops at a past point, not now.
"Yesterday" is a finished time: ALICE + COPIED. A state from then to now: SHE + HAS BEEN.
HAS COPIED does not go with "yesterday", and WAS does not reach now.

Choose your partner
Zombiella or Alice. Whoever you do not choose stays with the frightened guests.
Trust Zombiella · find the payment

ACT II · 21:10 · WINTER GARDEN
The gardeners’ secret

Eira and Lina run the winter garden. Bram maintains the outside paths. Nim, their small stone-faced assistant, has been hiding biscuits in the planters. Rook, Bram’s shaggy mountain dog, has found every one. “We’ve visited the annex before,” Lina says. “But we went there last Tuesday for the old garden plans.”
Eira points across the lake. The annex is below the ballroom, hidden by trees. The windows you saw from outside belong to it.
Separate experience from one dated visit: “The sisters ___ the annex before. They ___ there last Tuesday.”
ARE VISITING is happening now, and HAVE BEEN does not go with "last Tuesday".
GO turns the dated visit into a present routine.
Experience up to now: THE SISTERS + HAVE VISITED. One finished, dated visit: THEY + WENT.
HAVE GONE does not go with the finished time "last Tuesday".
ACT II · 21:20 · THE LAKESIDE BOATHOUSE
A light below the waterline

Nemo runs the hotel’s lake boats. Professor Aronnax is studying the water; Nadia, Mara and Lia maintain his instruments. Nadia’s sensor shows the annex heating has stopped. Someone could be trapped in a room that is getting colder every minute. Mara has repaired the emergency boat engine. Lia is still searching for its spare battery.
Through the rain, you see three flashes from a low window. Then three more. Someone is asking for help.
Choose the completed repair and the unfinished search: “Mara ___ the engine; it works now. Lia ___ for the battery for twenty minutes and is still looking.”
HAS BEEN REPAIRING does not say the repair is done, and HAS FOUND says the search succeeded.
WAS REPAIRING leaves the repair in the past and unfinished, but the search is still going on now.
A finished result: MARA + HAS REPAIRED. Effort that goes on to now: LIA + HAS BEEN SEARCHING.
REPAIRS is a routine, and SEARCHED says the search is over.
ACT II · 21:30 · THE OLD BOATHOUSE LANDING
The hotel’s “ghosts”

Angus Tulloch, the boatman, and Dr Vass, the lake biologist, have brought guests in from the storm. Harbour officer Brannan is checking their names. Kirsty and Ewan Sinclair carry blankets while Sandy Weir ties up the boats. “White shapes in the annex!” Sinclair says. “Ghosts!”

Vass holds up a bedsheet. Staff have been moving old linen through the tunnel. Tulloch heard someone knocking behind the archive door, but the music upstairs drowned it out. The Docherty brothers secure the landing. Davie counts arrivals with the visiting sergeant. The Lennox family confirm the annex heating failed.
Explain the apparently empty landing: “When Brannan reached the landing, Tulloch ___ the guests inside. While Brannan checked their names, Vass ___ blankets.”
HAS TAKEN looks from now, not from the moment Brannan arrived.
The guests were already inside, so not WAS TAKING. Vass was in the middle of giving, so not HAD GIVEN.
Present forms cannot tell this past sequence.
Before Brannan arrived: TULLOCH + HAD TAKEN. In progress while he checked: VASS + WAS GIVING.
ACT II · 21:40 · THE OLD PLAN CABINET
The floor that never vanished

Tensing opens a cabinet of old plans. Walton, the hotel’s retired transport captain, remembers the numbering. The annex once had three levels of its own. Its bottom room was 309. Renovations joined that level to the main hotel’s basement. The Clockmaker, who maintains the lobby clock, knows the tunnel. Mouse can reach its narrow latch.
“I used to deliver bags there,” Tensing says. “Dark tunnels don’t worry me. I’m used to working in them.”
Choose a past habit that ended, then something familiar now: “Tensing ___ deliver bags to the annex. He ___ working in dark tunnels.”
A past habit that has ended: USED TO + verb. Something familiar now: BE USED TO + -ING.
WOULD can describe a past habit, but HAS USED TO is not English.
WAS USING TO and USES TO are not English forms.
This swaps them. IS USED TO needs a noun or -ING, and "used to working" is not the past-habit pattern.
ACT II · 21:50 · THE ARCHIVE THRESHOLD
Room 309
Cat, the hotel’s silent night cleaner, emerges from behind a shelf and nearly gives Watson a heart attack. “The door’s been locked since eight,” she says. “I heard the Count call for help.”

You slide your key into the outer door. It opens onto a passage. A second door has an electronic lock. Through its small window, Blocula holds up a folder: STAFF OWNERSHIP. He did not plan to sell everyone’s jobs. He planned to give the staff control of the hotel.
Describe a state continuing to now, then the earlier locking: “The door ___ locked since eight. Someone ___ it before Cat came down.”
WAS does not carry the locked state up to now, and LOCKS is a routine.
IS cannot carry "since eight", and HAS LOCKED does not place the locking before Cat came.
HAD BEEN stops at a past point, and IS LOCKING is happening now.
A state up to now: THE DOOR + HAS BEEN locked. Before a past event: SOMEONE + HAD LOCKED it.
NOTEBOOK · THE STAFF-OWNERSHIP FOLDER. Blocula is alive inside archive E-309. His folder concerns staff ownership, giving the buyer a motive to stop him.
ACT II · 22:00 · OUTSIDE THE ARCHIVE
The midnight clause

Blocula speaks through the glass. “Andreas asked me to inspect the old plans. He locked me in. He took my phone.” The folder contains the original staff-ownership agreement. A copy must reach the village registrar before midnight to cancel the sale. Manager Menzies, who arranged the deal, has told everyone the deadline cannot move.
The Count points to a second document: a structural survey declaring the hotel unsafe. Waldman says its measurements are impossible.
Choose an action in progress at a future time, then one completed before it: “At 23:30 the registrar ___ applications. By midnight, she ___ the office.”
This swaps them: the checking is in progress at 23:30, and the closing is complete by midnight.
HAS BEEN CHECKING and CLOSED look from now and from the past, not from future times.
In progress at a future time: THE REGISTRAR + WILL BE CHECKING. Complete by a deadline: SHE + WILL HAVE CLOSED.
CHECKS is a routine, and HAS CLOSED is a result now, not by midnight.
ACT II · 22:10 · THE GARDEN DOORS
A promise in the storm

A branch hits the glass roof. Outside, the old footbridge bends under wet snow. Bram orders everyone away from it. “Look at that beam,” Lina says. “It’s going to fall.” Eira grabs the first-aid bag. Tensing looks at your shaking hands and quietly offers to carry the folder when you get it out.
An expected event and a decision made now can both point to the future. They tell us different things about the speaker’s evidence and intention.
Use the usual evidence-based prediction and immediate-offer forms: “Look at the bending beam! It ___. Don’t worry; I ___ the folder for you.”
WAS GOING TO FALL looks back from the past, and CARRIED is past. We need a prediction and an offer now.
HAS FALLEN says the fall has happened, but the beam is still bending.
FALLS is a general fact or a timetable, and HAVE CARRIED looks back.
Evidence you can see: IT + IS GOING TO FALL. An offer made now: I + WILL CARRY.
ACT II · 22:20 · THE CABLE-CAR STATION
The last cable car

Walton checks the emergency transport timetable. The last downhill cable car leaves at 23:40, provided the wind stays below the limit. After that, the only road will be under snow. Jax has arranged to meet the registrar’s assistant at the lower station at 23:50. He shows you the confirmation on his phone.
The plan is tight, but possible. The real problem is getting Blocula and the original agreement out of the archive.
Choose the timetable form and the personal arrangement: “The last car ___ at 23:40. Jax ___ the assistant at 23:50; they have confirmed it.”
HAS MET says the meeting has already happened.
LEFT is past, and WILL HAVE MET looks back from a later time.
HAS LEFT is a result now, not tonight's timetable.
A timetable: THE LAST CAR + LEAVES. A confirmed arrangement: JAX + IS MEETING.
ACT II · 22:30 · THE MAINTENANCE BAY
Two things worth saving

Nadia finds a backup socket. Zombito can power the archive lock from the workshop, but the damaged circuit cannot run the lock and the document scanner together. Victor checks the temperature behind the glass. Blocula is shivering. Clerval prepares warm blankets. The Creature offers to hold the power cable in place.
Choose your priority: free the Count first, or scan the agreement first. Both can be done, but the first decision changes the rescue and the ending.
Choose an activity under way at a future moment, then an existing plan: “At eleven, Zombito ___ the circuit. He ___ use the backup socket; that is his plan.”
HAS TESTED is a result now, and WILL HAVE + "use" is not a verb form.
WILL HAVE TESTED makes the test finished by eleven, and HAS TO is a duty, not his plan.
In progress at a future moment: ZOMBITO + WILL BE TESTING. A plan already made: HE + IS GOING TO use.
HAD BEEN TESTING looks back from the past, and WAS GOING TO is an old plan that may not happen.
What gets power first?
The damaged circuit can power one of them at a time.
The lock · get Blocula out first
Protect the owner. The document can be scanned after the rescue.
The scanner · protect the agreement first
Secure an early copy, but leave Blocula in the cold for longer.
ACT II · 22:40 · THE ENGINE ROOM
The longest shift

Nemo brings a boat battery to keep the lights alive. Mara and Lia run a cable through the service tunnel. Nadia checks the current while Zombito talks them through every connection. “I started at seven,” he says. “At midnight I’ll have been working for five hours. Remind me never to accept an ‘easy’ evening shift again.”
You need a completed repair before the cable car leaves, not just five hours of effort.
Contrast duration up to a future time with completion before a deadline: “At midnight, Zombito ___ for five hours. By 23:20, he ___ the lock circuit.”
Duration up to a future time: ZOMBITO + WILL HAVE BEEN WORKING. Complete by a deadline: HE + WILL HAVE REPAIRED.
The first half is right, but WILL HAVE BEEN REPAIRING measures effort. It does not say the repair is finished.
WILL BE WORKING does not measure the five hours, and HAS REPAIRED looks from now.
WILL WORK does not add up five hours by midnight, and IS REPAIRING is happening now.
ACT III · 22:50 · THE PLAN CABINET
The buyer’s real plan

Waldman and Aronnax compare the survey with the building plans. Andreas measured a storage wall as if it supported the whole hotel. Kit finds a second set of plans: luxury apartments, with no staff rooms.

Before anyone noticed the mistake, Andreas was going to use the “unsafe” report to close the hotel cheaply. He had already arranged tomorrow’s meeting with a developer. The missing owner, the false report and the midnight deadline are parts of one scheme.
Describe an intention held in the past, then an arrangement completed before discovery: “Andreas ___ close the hotel. He ___ the developer’s meeting before Waldman found the error.”
WILL and ARRANGES look forward from now, not back to his plan.
A plan in the past: ANDREAS + WAS GOING TO close. Finished before the discovery: HE + HAD ARRANGED.
IS GOING TO and HAS ARRANGED look from now. We are looking back from the past.
HAS BEEN GOING TO is not English, and WAS ARRANGING leaves the arrangement unfinished.
ACT III · 23:00 · THE SIDE PASSAGE
Evidence from your partner

Your chosen partner returns, wet and breathless. The other has stayed with the worried guests, keeping Andreas from slipping away. Holmes asks you to read the document aloud. “Evidence only helps if we say exactly what it proves.” The archive lock is still being repaired. The false survey has already been copied and sent to Lestrade’s secure phone.
Contrast an ongoing passive action and a completed passive result: “The lock ___ now. The false survey ___ already, so Lestrade has a copy.”
WAS REPAIRED is finished and past, and IS BEING COPIED says the copy is not finished.
Work going on now: THE LOCK + IS BEING REPAIRED. A finished result now: THE SURVEY + HAS BEEN COPIED.
IS REPAIRED is a state or a routine, and WAS BEING COPIED does not say the copy is finished.
These are active forms: they make the lock and the survey do the repairing and the copying.

Zombiella unfolds a signed receipt. Andreas paid for a song to continue until 20:15, leaving himself time to reach the annex unnoticed. The receipt proves a planned distraction; the camera and lift log connect it to his movements.
Alice brings the signed key request. Andreas asked for access to E-309 at 19:55, although he later claimed never to have used the service lift. The signature connects him to the copied annex key.
ACT III · 23:10 · THE ARCHIVE LOCK
When the green light comes on

The circuit hums. Zombito raises one hand: nobody touches the door until its light turns green. The Creature braces the frame. Victor waits with blankets. Your earlier decision sets the order of events, but you still need a safe, clear instruction. A wrong tense could make the command sound as if the rescue has already happened.
Beyond the glass, Blocula stands back. He trusts you to get this right.
Give the real future instruction: “When the light ___ green, we ___ the door.”
OPENED is past, so it is no longer an instruction about what we will do.
After WHEN, for the future, use the present simple: WHEN THE LIGHT + TURNS, not WILL TURN.
After WHEN, the present simple: THE LIGHT + TURNS. The main clause: WE + WILL OPEN.
TURNED and HAVE OPENED are past and present perfect. Neither gives a future instruction.
You sent the first burst of power to the lock. Blocula will be brought out before you turn on the scanner. Victor approves. “A document can wait five minutes. A person should not have to.”
You sent the first burst of power to the scanner. The agreement is safe, but Blocula has spent longer in the cold. Victor prepares to treat him as soon as the lock releases.
ACT III · 23:18 · THE OPEN ARCHIVE
The signature under the dust
The lock clicks. Blocula steps out, shaking but alive. Elizabeth, the staff representative, and Justine, head housekeeper, meet him with a coat. Watson checks the original agreement.

It was signed last month, before Andreas offered to buy the hotel. The sale contract only applies if no earlier staff agreement is registered by midnight. That is why Andreas needed the Count silent tonight. Under the dust is the final page: every permanent member of staff owns a share.
William brings his sister Elizabeth a mug of tea and asks whether she will still have a job tomorrow. “That is exactly what we’re deciding,” she says.
Put the legal documents in order without changing their timing: “The staff ___ the agreement last month. By the time Andreas made his offer, Blocula ___ it too.”
WERE SIGNING leaves the signing unfinished, and HAS SIGNED looks from now.
IS SIGNING puts Blocula's signature in progress now, but the document is old.
"Last month" is a finished time: THE STAFF + SIGNED. Before the later offer: BLOCULA + HAD SIGNED.
"Last month" needs the past simple, and SIGNS is present.
NOTEBOOK · THE EARLIER SIGNED AGREEMENT. The staff and Blocula signed before Andreas made his offer. Registering the agreement before midnight will stop the sale.
ACT III · 23:22 · THE BALLROOM DOORS
The whole night, in order
Lestrade asks Andreas to stay. Blane stands by the door; Tito stops playing. Menzies admits he accepted the false survey without asking an independent engineer to check it.

You lay out the sequence: Andreas entered the lift at 20:02. Blocula joined him at 20:04. At 20:06 the lift reached the annex. Andreas locked the archive, then used the stairs to reach the terrace. “I was only protecting my investment,” he says. Nobody in the room looks reassured.
Build the sequence from the Count’s arrival: “When Blocula ___ the lift, Andreas ___ inside for two minutes.”
These forms look from now, not from 20:04.
The past point: BLOCULA + ENTERED. Activity up to that point: ANDREAS + HAD BEEN WAITING.
Present forms take the sequence out of the finished past.
The Count's entry is the reference point, so ENTERED. The waiting started earlier and went on until then: HAD BEEN WAITING.
ACT III · 23:26 · THE SECURITY DESK
What the camera actually proves

Andreas changes his story. “I’ve never locked anyone in a room.” Lestrade plays the recovered annex clip. At 20:07, Andreas is visible turning the outside lock and taking the Count’s phone from the shelf. The general denial cannot survive one clearly recorded event. Your partner’s document supports the camera; it does not replace it.
Lestrade secures the phone and the footage. Now the problem is getting the agreement down the mountain.
Contrast the denial about experience with the dated event that disproves it: “Andreas says he ___ anyone in. But at 20:07 tonight, he ___ the archive door from outside.”
Experience up to now: HE + HAS NEVER LOCKED. One dated event at 20:07: HE + LOCKED.
IS NEVER LOCKING is not the form for life experience, and HAD LOCKED needs another past point.
IS LOCKING is happening now, but the camera recorded a finished event.
NEVER LOCKS is a habit, and a finished clock time takes the past simple, not HAS LOCKED.
NOTEBOOK · THE 20:07 LOCK FOOTAGE. The camera shows Andreas locking the archive from outside and taking Blocula’s phone. This directly supports Blocula’s account.
ACT III · 23:30 · THE CABLE-CAR PLATFORM
The deadline is a place in time
Jax has the sealed agreement. Rabbit brings the final envelope from reception. Bram checks the wind meter; Walton keeps the cable car at the platform while Tensing checks every fastening.

The registrar’s assistant began waiting at 22:50. By 23:50, she will have been waiting for an hour. Your job is to make sure she is waiting for people who actually arrive. The car’s doors close in ten minutes. Jax looks back. “One last check. Have we got the right document?”
Express accumulated waiting and a completed future handover: “By 23:50, the assistant ___ for an hour. By 23:55, Jax ___ the agreement to her.”
Duration up to 23:50: THE ASSISTANT + WILL HAVE BEEN WAITING. Complete by 23:55: JAX + WILL HAVE GIVEN.
WILL WAIT does not measure the hour, and WILL BE GIVING leaves the handover in progress.
The first half is right, but WILL BE GIVING leaves the handover in progress at 23:55, not complete.
HAS WAITED and GAVE look from now and from the past, not from the future deadlines.
ACT III · 23:40 · WATCHING THE DESCENT
A condition worth understanding
The cable car pulls away. Eira and Lina watch its lights shrink against the mountain. Nobody speaks until Jax’s radio crackles: “Wind steady. We’re moving.”

Tensing explains the last condition. If the agreement reaches the registrar before midnight, the sale stops. If it arrives late, the staff will still have evidence of the crime, but the ownership dispute will take longer to settle. This is a real possibility tonight, not an imaginary future.
State the real condition and its expected result: “If Jax ___ in time, the registrar ___ the agreement tonight.”
A real future possibility: IF + JAX + ARRIVES, then THE REGISTRAR + WILL REGISTER.
